findings.title: CI uses python tooling but the repository has no python project
findings.explanation: job "quality" step #2 sets up or runs python tools, but no python source files or manifests were found in the scanned tree. Such steps usually check nothing (e.g. a linter over zero files) and give a false signal of coverage.
findings.suggestion: Replace these steps with checks for the languages the repository actually contains, or add the missing python project if it was expected.

findings.title: CI step masks failure of an install command
findings.evidence: pip install ruff pytest bandit || true
findings.explanation: `|| true` hides installation failures (job "quality" step "Install dev tools"); later steps may then run without their tools while the job still passes.
findings.suggestion: Remove `|| true` or handle the specific expected failure explicitly.

findings.title: CI step masks failure of a test/lint/scan command
findings.explanation: `ruff check .` is a test/lint/scan command, but `|| true` makes the step succeed even when it fails, so this check can never turn CI red (job "quality" step "Lint (ruff)").
findings.suggestion: Remove `|| true`. If the check is not ready to gate merges, run it in a separate, explicitly non-blocking job and say so in the job name.

findings.title: Comparative performance claim: "Better than llama.cpp"
findings.evidence: * Better than llama.cpp with quantum optimization
findings.explanation: RepoTruth found no way to verify this comparison statically. Such claims should be backed by a reproducible benchmark in the repository.
findings.suggestion: Link a benchmark (method, hardware, numbers) or remove the claim.

findings.title: 5 comment(s) describe behaviour as simulated/placeholder
findings.evidence: L167: // Simulate quantum gate application | L202: // Simulate inference with energy tracking | L220: // Simulate logit calculation | L316: // Simulate model loading
findings.explanation: The code's own comments say parts of it are simulated, stubbed, or for demo only. If the README or file header presents this as a working feature, the claim is not backed by this code.
findings.suggestion: Label the file as a prototype/demo, or replace the simulated sections with real implementations and tests.

findings.title: Link to missing file: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

findings.suggestion: Add the referenced file or fix/remove the link.

findings.title: README setup commands need package.json, which is missing
findings.evidence: npm install | npm start | npm test | npm run build
findings.explanation: These commands run in the repository root, which has no package.json, so following the README fails. A package.json exists elsewhere (repotruth/package.json); the README may just be missing a `cd`.
findings.suggestion: Point the instructions at the directory that actually contains the manifest.

findings.title: README says MIT, but LICENSE is Proprietary
findings.evidence: README.md: "This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details." vs LICENSE: Proprietary
findings.explanation: The README's license statement names MIT, while LICENSE matches Proprietary text. Users cannot tell which terms apply. Which one is correct is a legal/owner decision.
findings.suggestion: Have the copyright owner decide the intended license and align the README and LICENSE. RepoTruth never changes license files automatically.
